AUTHOR: Ahn
TITLE: Flounders Measurement System using Obtained Optical Images by AUV
REGION: Japan (AUV seafloor survey; site not stated)
SPECIES: Flounders (Pleuronectidae) vs rays, starfish, crab, fishing net, sea cucumber, seaweed, seafloor, other fish
DATA: AUV seafloor still images provided by National Maritime Research Institute; 3,406 training images, 10 evaluation images
V_EV: Sec. II.A: '(a) and (c) in Fig.2 are shown low visibility images which are affected by light attenuation and reflectance of seafloor'; altitudes 2.54-3.05 m (Table IV)
D2: 3,406 training images; 10 randomly selected evaluation images (disjointness not stated)
D_EV: Sec. III: 'For the evaluation randomly 10 images are selected' - no grouping or relation to training images stated.
R_EV: Sec. III: evaluation only on 10 images from the same AUV image set: 'randomly 10 images are selected'
E_EV: Sec. III.C: 'the estimated flounders length [pixel] are compared with the human counted flounders length [pixel]... The average of error is 6 [pixel]'
ARCH: Retinex enhancement + Sobel/morphology candidate selection + AlexNet classification + geometric length estimation
METR: Region selection error rate, recognition accuracy (vs human counts), length error (pixels)
NOTE: Very small evaluation (10 images, 23 flounders). Length compared with human pixel measurements on same images only; actual-length conversion via altitude shown for one example (27.1 cm), not validated. Candidate detection is non-learned; the CNN classifies candidates. C_ALL coded NR (not NA) because the study is a detection/measurement pipeline, not classification-only, and no threshold is reported. Mean RGB intensities of example images reported but not used as a visibility metric. Whether the 10 evaluation images are disjoint from the 3,406 training images is not stated.
